title: Maximizing Energy Efficiency in Spiking Neural Networks: A Dynamic Joint Pruning Framework
problem: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) face energy and computational efficiency challenges due to growing architectural complexity, requiring aggressive pruning that balances multiple sparsity dimensions simultaneously.
motivation: SNNs promise energy efficiency through event-driven computation, but existing pruning methods focus on single sparsity forms, missing the synergistic benefits of joint spatiotemporal and weight sparsity optimization.
method: The framework removes unnecessary parts from spiking neural networks to reduce energy use by combining three techniques. It uses multi-stage masking to precisely control when individual neurons fire, temporal attention batch normalization (TABN) that adjusts information flow over time with learnable time scaling (letting the network learn how fast to process time), and a dynamic sparse strategy that decides which parts to remove based on real-time synaptic operations (the actual computations between connected neurons).
key_novelty: The framework jointly adjusts both spike patterns over time (spatiotemporal spike sparsity) and connection strengths (weight sparsity) dynamically to minimize synaptic operations during inference.
contributions: Multi-stage masking mechanism for adaptive neuron firing threshold control
Temporal attention batch normalization (TABN) module with learnable time scaling factors
Dynamic sparse strategy that adjusts coefficients based on real-time computational impact
126.38× SOP compression on CIFAR-10 with minimal accuracy loss
primary_theme: Dynamic joint pruning of spatiotemporal and weight sparsity for energy-efficient SNN inference
